chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was in Kufa among you; every morning he would leave the palace early and circulate through the markets of Kufa, market by market. With him was a whip on his shoulder, which had two ends and was called 'Al-Sabayba'.

He would stop at the people of each market and call out: 'O group of merchants! Fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic!' When they heard his voice (peace be upon him), they would throw down what was in their hands, direct their hearts to him, and listen with their ears.

He would say (peace be upon him): 'Prioritize seeking Allah's choice (Istikhara), find blessings in ease, draw near to the buyers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, keep away from oaths, avoid lying, turn away from injustice, give justice to the oppressed, do not approach usury, fulfill the measure and the scale, do not deprive people of their goods, and do not wander in the land causing corruption.'
He would circulate through all the markets of Kufa, then return and sit for the people.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.السَّبِيبَةَ: A type of whip with two ends

ai.seo_question: What ethical advice did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) give to merchants in Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) active governance model in Kufa, where he personally inspected markets with the *sibbah* (a double-ended staff) to ensure justice and prevent exploitation. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the ruler's direct responsibility for economic ethics, linking commercial integrity to spiritual piety through specific prohibitions like *riba* and *ghish* (deception).
